reviews.name: Ferhat Ulu
reviews.text:
Camiye yardım etmek güzel bir şeydir. Ama insanın kendisine şu soruyu sorması gerekir: “Allah rızası için yaptığımı söylediğim bu iş, Allah’ın evine gelen insanları rahatsız ediyor mu?”

Cuma günü insanlar alışveriş yapmaya değil, Allah’ın huzuruna çıkmaya geliyor. Siz ise namaz vaktinin hemen öncesinde lahmacunları insanların gözünün önünde pişirip kokusunu caminin içine kadar yayıyorsunuz. İnsanların burnunun dibinde satış yapılıyor, bazıları 20 tane alıp götürüyor; sonunda namaz kılmaya gelen insanlara bir lahmacun bile kalmıyor.

Sonra da bunun adına “camiye yardım” deniliyor.

Allah Teâlâ Cuma suresinde şöyle buyuruyor:

“Cuma günü namaz için çağrı yapıldığı zaman Allah’ın zikrine koşun ve alışverişi bırakın.”
(Cuma, 62/9)

Bir düşünün: Ayette Cuma vaktinde alışverişi bırakmak emredilirken, siz insanların Allah’ın zikrine yöneldiği anda caminin önünü satış yerine çeviriyorsunuz.

Elbette camiye yardım edilebilir. Ama Allah’ın evinin hürmetini zedeleyerek yapılan bir yardımın usulünü de sorgulamak gerekir.

Kur’an bize israfı ve ölçüsüzlüğü de hatırlatır:

“Yiyin, için fakat israf etmeyin. Çünkü Allah israf edenleri sevmez.”
(A‘râf, 7/31)

Bir kişinin ihtiyacından çok daha fazlasını alıp götürmesi, başkasının hiçbir şey alamaması ve bunun normal görülmesi de “hayır” anlayışının ne kadar adil olduğunu düşündürmelidir.

Şunu da unutmayın:

Caminin adı bir reklam tabelası değildir.
Cami, satış yapmak için kullanılacak bir pazar yeri değildir.
Hayır adı altında yapılan her iş, sırf camiye para kazandırıyor diye kutsal hâle gelmez.

Allah’ın evine yardım edecekseniz, önce Allah’ın evinin hürmetini koruyun. Namaz kılmaya gelen insanın huzurunu bozmayın. Cuma gününü ticari faaliyetin gölgesinde bırakmayın. İnsanların burnuna yemek kokusu tüttürüp sonra “camiye yardım ediyoruz” demek yerine, yardımın gerçekten edebine, adaletine ve niyetine bakın.

Çünkü Allah sadece ne yaptığımıza değil, nasıl yaptığımıza ve niyetimize de bakar.

Bir lahmacun satıp camiye para kazandırmak kolaydır.
Asıl mesele, Allah’ın evinin hürmetini koruyarak hayır yapabilmektir.

Bunu yapan herkes kendisine dürüstçe sorsun:

“Ben gerçekten camiye hizmet mi ediyorum, yoksa caminin adını kullanarak yaptığım ticareti mi meşrulaştırıyorum?”

Bu sorunun cevabını insanlardan değil, Allah’tan saklayamazsınız.
reviews.textTranslated:
Helping the mosque is a good thing. But one should ask oneself: “Does this act, which I claim to be doing for the sake of Allah, disturb the people who come to the house of Allah?”

On Friday, people come to stand before Allah, not to shop. Yet, you are baking lahmacun (a type of Turkish pizza) right before people's eyes, spreading its aroma throughout the mosque. Sales are taking place right under people's noses; some buy 20 and take them away, leaving not even one lahmacun for those who come to pray.

And then this is called "helping the mosque."

Allah Almighty says in Surah Al-Jumu'ah:

“When the call to prayer is made on Friday, hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave off your business.” (Al-Jumu'ah, 62/9)

Think about it: While the verse commands that one should stop shopping at Friday prayer time, you are turning the area in front of the mosque into a place of sale at a time when people are devoting themselves to the remembrance of Allah.

Of course, helping the mosque is permissible. But we must also question the method of giving aid in a way that undermines the sanctity of God's house.

The Quran reminds us of extravagance and excess:

“Eat and drink, but do not be extravagant. Indeed, Allah does not love those who are extravagant.” (Al-A'raf, 7/31)

The fact that one person takes far more than they need, while another receives nothing, and this is considered normal, should make us question the fairness of the concept of "charity."

Also, remember this:

The name of a mosque is not an advertising sign.
A mosque is not a marketplace to be used for selling goods.
Not every act of charity becomes sacred simply because it generates income for the mosque.

If you are going to help God's house, first protect the sanctity of God's house. Do not disturb the peace of those who come to pray. Do not overshadow Friday with commercial activity. Instead of filling people's noses with the smell of food and then saying, "We're helping the mosque," look at the true etiquette, justice, and intention of the help.

Because God looks not only at what we do, but also at how we do it and our intentions.

Selling a lahmacun (Turkish pizza) and raising money for the mosque is easy. The real issue is being able to do good while respecting the sanctity of God's house.

Everyone who does this should honestly ask themselves:

"Am I truly serving the mosque, or am I legitimizing my business by using the mosque's name?"

You cannot hide the answer to this question from God, not from people.

Sowohl im Hinterhof als auch vorne an der Bushaltestelle wird sich regelmäßig sehr laut unterhalten und verhalten, wodurch die Anwohner erheblich gestört werden.

Ich bitte Sie daher dringend, darauf zu achten, dass insbesondere abends Rücksicht auf die Anwohner genommen und die Lautstärke deutlich reduziert wird. Es ist auf Dauer nicht zumutbar, dass man in der eigenen Wohnung bis spät abends durch laute Gespräche und Lärm gestört wird.

Sollte sich die Situation nicht verbessern und die Ruhestörungen weiterhin regelmäßig auftreten, sehe ich mich gezwungen, die Polizei bzw. das zuständige Ordnungsamt zu verständigen.
reviews.textTranslated:
I would like to complain about the repeated and sometimes significant noise disturbances in the vicinity of the mosque.

The disturbances occur both during the week and on weekends, especially in the evenings. At times, it is very loud until 10 or even 11 p.m. There is regular loud talking and behavior both in the courtyard and at the bus stop, which significantly disturbs the residents.

I therefore urge you to ensure that consideration is shown to the residents, especially in the evenings, and that the noise level is significantly reduced. It is unacceptable to be disturbed in one's own home by loud conversations and noise until late at night.

Should the situation not improve and the disturbances continue to occur regularly, I will be forced to contact the police or the relevant public order office.

reviews.name: Atiyye
reviews.text:
Die Gebetsräume befinden sich in der Kulturetage 3.OG. Eine Wegbeschreibung gibt es leider nicht.
Die Gebetsbereiche für Frauen und Männer sind getrennt und jeweils mit einem Waschbereich für Abdest/Wudu ausgestattet. Die Räume sind sehr hell, schön und ansprechend eingerichtet. Gebetsteppiche und Gebetskleidung sind vorhanden.
Besonders praktisch, wenn man unterwegs ist und die Gebetszeit eintritt. Insgesamt ein sehr schöner und angenehmer Ort zum Beten. Im Sommer wäre allerdings ein Ventilator oder eine andere Möglichkeit zur Kühlung wünschenswert, da es in den Räumen relativ warm ist.
reviews.textTranslated:
The prayer rooms are located on the third floor of the cultural center. Unfortunately, there are no directions provided.

The prayer areas for women and men are separate and each has its own ablution/Wudu area. The rooms are very bright, beautiful, and attractively furnished. Prayer rugs and prayer clothes are provided.

This is especially convenient when you're traveling and prayer time arrives. Overall, it's a very nice and pleasant place to pray. However, a fan or some other form of cooling would be desirable in the summer, as the rooms can get quite warm.

ownerDescription: Die Afghanische Gemeinde München ist ein Ort des Gebets, des Lernens und der Gemeinschaft für Muslime in München und Umgebung.

ownerUpdates.text:
Gemeinsam für unsere Moschee – Jede Spende zählt

Im Namen Allahs, des Allerbarmers, des Barmherzigen.

Unsere Moschee ist mehr als nur ein Gebetsort. Sie ist ein Ort der Gemeinschaft, des Wissens, der Erziehung unserer Kinder und des Zusammenhalts. Hier finden Menschen Trost, Orientierung und die Möglichkeit, ihren Glauben gemeinsam zu leben.

Um unsere Moschee zu erhalten, auszubauen und zukünftigen Generationen zu übergeben, sind wir auf die Unterstützung unserer Gemeinschaft angewiesen. Jeder Beitrag – ob groß oder klein – hilft dabei, dieses wertvolle Haus Allahs zu stärken.

Der Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) sagte:

"Wer für Allah eine Moschee baut, dem baut Allah ein Haus im Paradies."

Mit deiner Spende investierst du nicht nur in Steine und Mauern, sondern in einen Ort des Gebets, des Lernens und der guten Taten, von dem viele Menschen profitieren werden.

Unterstütze unsere Moschee noch heute.
Jeder Euro macht einen Unterschied.
